title: Session fidelity stability primer and migration checklist
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This primer explains best practices for preserving session-level fidelity across platform changes (model variant swaps, quantization rollouts, runtime kernel updates, and cache population strategies). It also provides a customer migration checklist and a minimal telemetry contract that product and SRE teams should adopt before any fidelity-impacting release. Target audience: product managers, platform engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers.

Why session fidelity matters

- User experience: abrupt changes in response style, hallucination rate, or token-level length can break downstream UX and automated evaluation suites.
- SLAs: many customers bind SLAs to response consistency (not just latency). Degraded fidelity can cause escalations even when latencies improve.
- Billing & quotas: quality regressions often correlate with increased token usage (retries, longer completions).

Goals of this document

1. Define stability targets and guardrails for session fidelity during platform changes.
2. Provide a reproducible migration checklist for customers and internal rollout owners.
3. Standardize a minimal telemetry contract for fidelity-related signals.

Stability targets and metrics

- Target response-consistency SLO: 95% of sessions must have a fidelity delta below the configured threshold per tenant (default threshold = 0.12 comparative perplexity / BLEU-style score equivalent).
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile <= pre-change baseline + 25ms for interactive sessions.
- Regression alert thresholds (trigger automated rollback candidate):
  - Delta in primary eval metric > 10% on canary promptset,
  - Increase in session retry rate > 2 percentage points,
  - End-user error reports > 5 / 1k sessions in 1 hour.

Key signals (must be collected per-route and per-tenant):

- promptset_id (string), session_id (uuid), model_variant (string), model_version (string)
- baseline_eval_score (float), live_eval_score (float), score_delta (float)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (0-1), batching_size (int), latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (int)
- token_count_request, token_count_response, retry_count
- user_feedback_signal (enum: thumbs_up|thumbs_down|none), fallback_triggered (bool)

Migration checklist (pre-release for any fidelity-impacting change)

Owner: release owner (product/platform) — runbook must be followed before canary and GA.

1. Define the scope and downgrade surface
   - Catalog routes affected (API endpoints, sandbox environments, streaming vs non-streaming).
   - List known downstream consumers (webhooks, long-running jobs).
2. Assemble canary promptset and golden traces
   - Minimum 250 prompts covering short/long contexts, instruction vs chat, and edge cases (safety, numeric precision, code).
   - Add 50 customer-supplied prompts where available (obfuscate PII).
3. Baseline evaluation and statistical guardrails
   - Run baseline_eval_score across current production variant; record metrics per-tenant.
   - Define per-tenant tolerance buckets: conservative (0.05), standard (0.12), experimental (0.20).
4. Telemetry contract verification
   - Confirm collectors emit required keys (see Telemetry contract section).
   - Ensure 7-day retention for full fidelity signals and 90-day aggregate retention for trending.
5. Run synthetic traffic & cold-start scenarios
   - Simulate typical and burst traffic for 24 hours with injected cold starts.
   - Validate KV cache warmup helpers and adaptive-batching logic behave within cost/latency budget.
6. Canary rollout (tiered)
   - Canary #1: internal-only traffic (routing tag = internal_canary) for 2 hours.
   - Canary #2: 5% sampled production traffic with priority isolation for 12 hours.
   - Canary #3: 25% tenant-level rollout for 48 hours; include small number of friendly customer tenants with SLO addenda.
7. Monitor & decision gates
   - Real-time dashboard: compare live_eval_score to baseline by promptset; watch score_delta and retry_count.
   - If any regression alert threshold breaches, trigger automated rollback policy.
8. Post-rollout validation and customer comms
   - Run a full audit of golden traces and send a summary to affected tenant owners.
   - Publish migration notes in the release changelog with recommended mitigations for customer overrides (pin model_version, increase tolerance bucket).

Telemetry contract (minimum required fields)

The telemetry contract below is the minimal set of signals every runtime change must respect. Each signal should be emitted as a single event per completed response and as aggregate metrics for streaming partials.

Required event fields (flat keys):
| field | type | description |
|---|---:|---|
| timestamp | iso8601 string | event time (UTC) |
| tenant_id | string | tenant identifier |
| route | string | API route or route_alias |
| session_id | string | session identifier |
| promptset_id | string | canonical promptset used for evaluation |
| model_variant | string | e.g. redwood-v2-13b-q4 |
| model_version | string | pinned model version id |
| baseline_eval_score | float | production baseline score for promptset |
| live_eval_score | float | current score for this response |
| score_delta | float | live_eval_score - baseline_eval_score |
| kv_cache_hit_rate | float | 0.0 - 1.0 |
| tokens_in | int | request tokens |
| tokens_out | int | response tokens |
| latency_ms | int | end-to-end request latency |
| fallback_triggered | bool | whether a fallback model/region was used |

Suggested aggregate metrics (exported minute-by-minute):
- median_score_delta_by_route, p95_latency_ms_by_route, retry_rate_by_tenant, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_tenant, feedback_rate_by_route

Example minimal telemetry event (JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-28T14:12:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "session_id": "c3a9f2e4-1b2c-4d3e-9f0a-123456789abc",
  "promptset_id": "canary-2026-02-b",
  "model_variant": "redwood-v4-70b-q8",
  "model_version": "v4-2026-02-18",
  "baseline_eval_score": 0.86,
  "live_eval_score": 0.84,
  "score_delta": -0.02,
  "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.72,
  "tokens_in": 42,
  "tokens_out": 128,
  "latency_ms": 178,
  "fallback_triggered": false
}

Operational mitigations and quick fixes

- Immediate rollback: automated if primary canary thresholds breach. Owners should escalate to platform SRE on any manual rollback.
- Scoped rollback: revert model_version for affected route while leaving global runtime updates in place.
- Band-aid customer toggles: provide tenant-level flags for tolerance_bucket and pin_model_version in the console.
- Quality warmup: for quantization patches, a staged warmup that runs golden traces through a correction shim (lightweight re-ranking) for 6 hours can bridge gaps.

Customer migration notes (template to send to customers)

Subject: Upcoming fidelity-stability update and recommended actions

- What we’re changing: brief bullet describing the model/runtime change.
- Why: short rationale and expected benefits (latency/cost/throughput).
- Customer action (recommended): pin model_version if you require bit-for-bit outputs; otherwise choose conservative tolerance_bucket.
- If you observe regressions: collect session exports (session_id list), turn on enhanced logging, and open a support ticket with tags: fidelity-investigation, tenant-<id>.

Appendix A — Example policy YAML: per-tenant tolerance and canary schedule\n
policy_name: session_fidelity_migration_v1
owners:
  - product: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
  - platform_sre: marcus.greene@redwood.ai
tolerance_buckets:
  conservative: 0.05
  standard: 0.12
  experimental: 0.20
canary_schedule:
  internal: 120m
  sampled_production: 12h
  tenant_stage: 48h
rollback_thresholds:
  score_delta_pct: 10
  retry_delta_points: 2
  feedback_rate_per_1k: 5

Appendix B — Quick prompts for golden traces (examples)
1) API instruction: "Summarize the below policy in two bullets, preserve numeric thresholds:" + policy text.
2) Long-context completion: 8+ paragraph technical note, ask for a 3-paragraph executive summary.
3) Numeric precision: arithmetic chains of 8 operations with mixed floats and integers.
4) Safety edge-case: refusal correctness with adversarial phrasing.

Appendix C — Ownership and escalation
- Release owner: product (primary contact in policy).
- Canary monitoring: platform-sre (on-call rotation).
- Customer comms & escalation: customer-success for impacted tenants.

Related artifacts and links
- Canary promptset generator (internal notebook): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/canary-promptset-generator
- Fidelity regression dashboard (Grafana): grafana.internal.redwood/company/fidelity-regressions
- Telemetry schema repo: git@internal:redwood/telemetry-schema.git

Summary

Preserving session fidelity is a cross-functional challenge requiring clear metric definitions, reproducible promptsets, and a short, enforceable rollout playbook. This document should be used as the baseline checklist for any fidelity-affecting change. For questions or to propose updates, open a PR against this page and loop in platform-sre and product reviewers listed above.
